_about: Arius's challenge cards. 'counters' lists the player card ids that answer this challenge correctly. 'unlocksSlot' is the Creed slot filled when the player answers correctly. 'power' is how many bishops Arius gains if the challenge goes unanswered. 'explanation' is the popup after the clash: the right reading, 2-3 sentences.

cards.name: The Lord Created Me
cards.text: Arius: Wisdom says 'The Lord created me.' The Son is Wisdom. So the Son was created!
cards.flavor: The Lord created me a beginning of His ways, for His works
cards.explanation: Proverbs speaks in riddles, so Athanasius says to ask who is speaking, and when. 'Created' points to the human body the Son took on to save us, not to His Godhead. As God, He is the One through whom all things were made.

quote.text: My Father has prepared for Me a body, and has created Me for men in behalf of their salvation.

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians II.44-47
cards.note: Verse text is as Athanasius quotes it in Against the Arians II.44. Arius relied on the Greek 'created'; the NKJV, from the Hebrew, reads 'The LORD possessed me.'

cards.name: Firstborn Over All Creation
cards.text: Arius: 'Firstborn over all creation.' First of the creatures is still a creature!
cards.explanation: 'Firstborn' doesn't mean the first thing made. The very next verse says all things were created by Him. He is the Only-begotten Son, and He is called 'Firstborn' because He became a Brother to us.

quote.text: because of the Word's condescension to the creatures, according to which He has become the 'Brother' of 'many.'

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians II.62-63
cards.note: Arius read the Greek 'firstborn of all creation.' The NKJV's 'over all creation' already leans toward the Orthodox reading, which may make this challenge feel easier.

cards.name: Greater Than I
cards.text: Arius: Jesus Himself said the Father is greater. So the Son is lesser!
cards.flavor: My Father is greater than I.
cards.explanation: Jesus said 'greater,' not 'better.' Athanasius explains that the Father is greater because the Son is begotten from Him, not because the Son is a lesser kind of being. The same Jesus said, 'I and my Father are one.'

quote.text: 'greater,' not indeed in greatness, nor in time, but because of His generation from the Father Himself

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians I.58
cards.note: This follows Athanasius's own reading (the Father as source). Other Fathers also read this verse as spoken in Christ's humanity; the brief's original explanation used that reading.

cards.name: Not Even the Son Knows
cards.text: Arius: The Son doesn't know the day or hour. God knows everything. So the Son isn't God!
cards.flavor: But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
cards.explanation: The Son truly became man, and He speaks sometimes as God and sometimes as man. Not knowing the hour belongs to the human nature He took on for us, not to the Word who made the world.

quote.text: He made this as those other declarations as man by reason of the flesh

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians III.42-43

cards.name: The Only True God
cards.text: Arius: Jesus called the Father 'the only true God.' That leaves the Son out!
cards.flavor: that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
cards.explanation: 'Only true God' is said against false gods, not against the Son. Jesus even names Himself right next to the Father in the same sentence. And John calls the Son Himself 'the true God.'

quote.text: this is said not to the denial of Him who said, 'I am the Truth,'

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians III.9

cards.name: God Made Him Lord
cards.text: Arius: 'God has MADE Him Lord.' If He was made Lord, He wasn't Lord before!
cards.flavor: God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ.
cards.explanation: Read the whole verse: 'this Jesus, whom you crucified.' Peter is talking about the Son as man, shown to be Lord after the Cross, not about when the Son began. He is forever the radiance of the Father's glory.

quote.text: provided they attend to the context

cards.citation: St. Athanasius, Against the Arians II.12

cards.name: Once He Was Not
cards.text: Arius: A father exists before his son. So there was a time when the Son did not exist!
cards.explanation: If the Son once didn't exist, then God was once without His own Word and Wisdom, like a light with no shine. But God has always been Father, so He has always had His Son.
cards.citation: Creed of Nicaea (325), anathemas; St. Athanasius, Against the Arians I.5, I.14
cards.note: The slogan's wording is from the anathemas of the 325 Creed. The quote shows Athanasius reporting Arius's own words from the Thalia.

cards.name: He Came to Be From Nothing
cards.text: Arius: God made everything from nothing, and that includes the Son.
cards.flavor: He came to be from nothing.
cards.explanation: Anything made from nothing is a creature, and a creature can't rescue creation. Only the Word who made all things out of nothing could make us new again.

quote.text: Who, save the Word of God Himself, Who also in the beginning had made all things out of nothing?

cards.citation: Creed of Nicaea (325), anathemas; St. Athanasius, On the Incarnation §7
